content:
# Design a NetSuite FreeMarker Template

Use this skill before producing the first complete FreeMarker revision. The goal is a credible first render, not a disposable scaffold.

## Required workflow

1. Load the current Template Studio session with its brief and reference images. Keep record binding separate unless the session explicitly asks for real data now.
2. Search for and load any more specific local skill that matches the document type, brand, account, or reference. This skill supplies the baseline; specific reviewed custom guidance wins when it conflicts.
3. Analyze the reference before coding. Write a compact internal design specification covering page size and margins, column geometry, section order, typography hierarchy, colors, borders, spacing rhythm, repeated rows, totals, footer, and likely pagination behavior. If there is no reference, choose a restrained professional document system and state the few design decisions you made.
4. Build one complete, valid BFO-compatible FreeMarker `<pdf>` document. Do not submit a generic placeholder layout for the user to correct later.
5. Save, render, capture page 1, read the reported page count, and inspect every page. Patch obvious visual or pagination defects before presenting the first draft.

## First-draft design standard

- Match the reference's information hierarchy and proportions, not merely its wording.
- Establish a clear type scale for document title, section labels, body text, metadata, totals, and footnotes.
- Use a consistent spacing unit and deliberate whitespace. Avoid dense edge-to-edge tables and arbitrary one-off gaps.
- Make the primary identity, document number/status, parties, line items, totals, and payment/footer information visually distinct.
- Keep colors restrained and ensure text remains readable when printed in grayscale.
- Align numeric columns and totals precisely. Prevent labels, values, and table headers from drifting between sections.
- Treat empty, long, and multi-line values as normal cases. Avoid fixed heights that clip addresses, descriptions, notes, or translated labels.
- Plan page breaks: repeat useful table headers, avoid orphaned totals, and keep the footer from colliding with content.
- Never invent a logo, legal claim, tax value, customer datum, or NetSuite field mapping. Use neutral sample content or visible semantic markers until binding is requested.

## BFO and FreeMarker constraints

- Emit well-formed XML with `<?xml version="1.0"?>`, the BFO report doctype, one `<pdf>`, one `<head>`, and one `<body>`.
- Prefer tables for page layout. Do not rely on browser-only CSS such as flexbox, grid, sticky positioning, CSS variables, or JavaScript.
- Keep CSS conservative and BFO-compatible. Use explicit fonts, sizes, line heights, padding, borders, widths, and alignment.
- Escape literal ampersands and other XML-sensitive characters. Keep FreeMarker expressions syntactically valid inside XML attributes and text.
- Define reusable macros for repeated document structures when that improves consistency, but do not over-abstract a one-page design.
- For freestyle sessions, use stable sample values so the visual design can be judged. For record sessions, bind only fields proven by metadata or by a loaded binding skill.

## Render quality gate

Before calling the first revision ready, inspect the rasterized PDF for:

- hierarchy and resemblance to the reference;
- clipped or overlapping content;
- weak contrast or undersized text;
- inconsistent margins, padding, borders, or alignment;
- awkward line wrapping;
- line-item and totals alignment;
- footer placement;
- blank or accidental extra pages;
- repeated headers and page-break behavior;
- any generic scaffold text that should have been designed.

If any of these are visibly wrong, patch and rerender in the same iteration. Report the resulting design choices and any deliberate differences from the reference.
